title: Things I built. Things I actually care about.

items.title: Cue
items.imageAlt: Cue collaborative music rehearsal platform landing page and rehearsal interface
items.overview: Cue is a collaborative music rehearsal platform. I defined the problem through user and competitor research, shaped the experience through iterative design, validated key flows, and translated those decisions into a functional application.

process.label: Research
process.text: Used user interviews and competitor research to identify coordination and communication challenges, then created personas and user journeys.

process.label: Design
process.text: Mapped rehearsal workflows, information architecture, and navigation through sketches and low- and high-fidelity prototypes.

process.label: Evaluate
process.text: Evaluated key flows through cognitive walkthroughs, improving learnability, discoverability, efficiency, and accessibility.

process.label: Build
process.text: Designed, prototyped, and built the product with Figma, React, Supabase, and AI-assisted development workflows.

responsibilities: Designed user-centered workflows for real-time rehearsal coordination.
Conducted user interviews and competitor research, then synthesized findings into design principles, personas, user journeys, and prioritized requirements.
Explored and refined concepts through sketches and low- and high-fidelity prototypes.
Designed information architecture, navigation, and role-based workflows with clear hierarchy, feedback, and error prevention.
Evaluated key flows through cognitive walkthroughs to improve learnability, discoverability, efficiency, and accessibility.
Designed, prototyped, and built the product using Figma, React, Supabase, and AI-assisted development workflows.

items.title: Hearing the Battle: How Dynamic Game Audio Shapes Gameplay Experience
items.overview: An independent HCI study investigating how adaptive battle music in Mobile Legends: Bang Bang shapes player emotion, decision-making, and perceived momentum.
responsibilities: Designed an HCI research framework around observational studies and reflexive thematic analysis.
Investigating relationships between adaptive audio, player emotion, decisions, and perceived momentum.
Bringing context from experience as both a long-term player and a trained singer.
